messages:
maya: quick sync — onboarding nova13b. I ran the conversion to safetensors locally, but before we flip to dedicated/hosted I want a quick check on: final S3 path, shard naming/TP layout, tokenizer quirks (we saw odd BOS), and whether we should serve FP16 or BF16. Attached conversion log below.

trent: put the final artifacts here: s3://redwood-prod-models/onboard/nova13b/2026-03-15/ 
- file pattern: nova13b-000.safetensors ... nova13b-012.safetensors (13 shards)
- index: nova13b.index.json present
Naming convention: {model}-{shard_idx}.safetensors.
TP layout: production config expects tensor_parallel=2, so there are two TP shards per device group. If you converted with TP=1 we need to remap.

li: tokenizer note: the checkpoint uses a custom BOS token id 50256 (not standard). HF loader maps BOS to 50256 and no PAD was defined, which breaks batching in our runtime. I added a tiny patch to the tokenizer config to set pad_token="<pad>" and pad_token_id=50257. Also set bos_token_id=50256 explicitly. Example patch:
```json
{
  "bos_token": "",
  "bos_token_id": 50256,
  "pad_token": "<pad>",
  "pad_token_id": 50257
}
```
Test: tokenizing "Hello" before patch -> [50256, 15496, ...], after patch -> [50256, 15496, ...] and batching works.

sam: conversion command I used for reference: 
`python convert_checkpoint.py --src checkpoints/nova13b --out /tmp/nova-safetensors --dtype fp16 --tp 2 --safetensors`
Then build index: `python build_index.py /tmp/nova-safetensors --out nova13b.index.json`
I kept bias/LayerNorm as fp32 with `--keep-bias-fp32` because tiny perf/accuracy tradeoff.

maya: for Dedicated we default to fp16 unless eval shows >0.5% regression on our eval set. Can someone run a quick eval sweep (5 prompts, 3 seeds) and paste numbers? @trent? :eyes:

trent: starting eval now, ETA ~25m. Quick FYI — one shard had mismatched checksum after the first pack (packerd v0.9 bug). I re-ran packer with `--fix-align` and checksums match. Also verified shard sizes: 13 shards, roughly equal except last ~40MB smaller which is expected due to final tensor packing. ops-bot: artifact-scan: 13 shards detected, index verified, checksum pass. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: deploy-checker: artifact s3://redwood-prod-models/onboard/nova13b/2026-03-15/ passed quick QA: size-check OK, index present, 13 shards, tensor_parallel declared = 2.

li: small tokenizer edge-case: during greedy decoding we saw stray leading token when pad_token_id wasn't set (off-by-one in batching). After adding pad_token it's consistent. Also bump vocab_size in config to 50258 to match final tokenizer.

sam: PR opened for the convert script and index builder -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/models/pull/4567. Includes a smoke test that loads all shards with HF->runtime loader and runs a single forward pass. Please review.

maya: thanks. Once eval finishes and @sam's PR is green, can we do a canary with 5% traffic to Dedicated? Also add a fallback route to nova13b-quant (lower perf) if latency spikes.

trent: eval results: mean-accuracy delta = +0.1% (within noise), latency median ~ 78ms tok/slice on test bench (tp=2, fp16). No major regressions. I'm happy to greenlight canary.

li: ran tokenizer smoke tests — all samples match golden tokens. I pushed the tokenizer config update to the artifact path (same S3) and updated index.json to reference it.

maya: awesome. @sam can you cut the CR for the rollout (canary -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%) and add rollback on error >5% or latency 2x? :thumbsup:

sam: will do, CR created and assigned to @trent. PR and runbook linked in the CR.

trent: rolling canary scheduled in 30m. tagging infra team for capacity: @infra-signal FYI.

maya: thanks everyone. Quick postmortem note if anything pops up: keep a checklist for next model onboarding: 1) tokenizer pad/bos/pad ids, 2) TP layout sanity, 3) index present, 4) checksum, 5) smoke eval. I'll draft and share.

sam: noted — will add to onboarding checklist doc. :memo:
